title: LinkedIn Links Move to the First Comment, Not the Post | vitalii.no
description:
Every post sent to LinkedIn carried a raw vitalii.no link right in the body — exactly the kind of outbound link that LinkedIn's own algorithm is suspected of quietly suppressing. Facebook's post body had a similar problem: no fixed order for the link, the source, and the hashtags.

post-to-linkedin was rewritten so the body never contains the URL: the post publishes first, then a new commentOnLinkedInPost function in _shared/linkedin-helpers.ts drops the article link into a comment on the fresh post, retrying up to three times if it fails. post-to-facebook now enforces a fixed order — body text, the vitalii.no link, the source domain instead of a raw URL, then the hashtag block last.

The comment step retries up to three times before giving up, and the actual post content sent is now stored for audit. Both rewritten social teaser prompts are backed up so the wording can be rolled back without touching code.
